system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: In MVFA's few-shot inference, the released code min-max normalises the zero-shot (text) branch and the few-shot (memory-bank) branch with the minimum and maximum over the entire test set and adds them with a fixed weight of 0.5, so the score of one image depends on the rest of the test set and a single incoming image cannot be scored. Can this transductive normalisation be replaced by an inductive one computed only from the K normal support images, at a small cost in AUROC? The inductive normaliser maps each branch's patch scores through the 1st and 99th percentiles of the leave-one-out patch scores of the supports (every patch of support i scored against the memory bank of the other K-1 supports and against the text anchors), which gives thousands of reference values even at K = 2; the fusion weight and the max pooling of the image score are kept fixed. Primary outcome: image-level and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive normalisation on each held-out BMAD dataset for K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the original method's AUROC across random half-size test subsets and at shifted prevalence (10% and 50% abnormal). Secondary outcome: sensitivity at 95% specificity with a threshold fixed from the support scores alone.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Position-wise low anchor and synthetic high anchor for inductive MVFA scoring
SUMMARY: Normalise each branch per grid position between a shrunk position-wise median of leave-one-out support scores (low anchor) and the median score of synthetic lesions pasted into the supports (high anchor), keeping MVFA's 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
HYPOTHESIS: On spatially aligned held-out modalities, the position-wise/synthetic two-anchor normaliser keeps image and pixel AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline at K >= 4 and improves pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over global support percentiles.
RATIONALE: The position-wise parent removes anatomy-driven offsets but has no principled upper scale; the synthetic-anchor parent gives an upper scale but treats all positions alike. Using the position-wise statistic as the low anchor and the synthetic lesion score as a global high anchor gives a normaliser that is both anatomy-aware and on a common scale across branches, without any test-set statistic.
METHOD: 1) utils.py: positional_low(support_maps): per-position LOO medians with 3x3 neighbourhood and shrinkage 20 towards the global median; synthetic_high(model, supports): 20 Poisson-blended lesions per support (1-5% area), median lesion-pixel score per branch and level. 2) test_few.py: z = clip((s_j - lo_j)/(hi - lo_j), -1, 3) rescaled to [0, 1]; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baselines: position-wise only; synthetic two-anchor only. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, per-position false-positive maps. Falsified if no gain over global percentiles on aligned modalities.

Idea B:
TITLE: Anchor-geometry normalisation of MVFA's zero-shot branch
SUMMARY: Replace the softmax output of the zero-shot branch by the patch projection on the unit anchor-difference direction, standardise both branches with support LOO statistics, and fuse them with MVFA's unchanged rule.
HYPOTHESIS: Standardising the unit-direction projection makes the support-derived threshold transfer across held-out modalities with a realised-specificity spread at least 5 points smaller than with percentile-normalised softmax scores, at equal AUROC (within 1 point).
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: zero-shot branch representation and normaliser (test-set min-max on softmax; support percentiles on softmax; support standardisation of the unit-direction projection). For level l: u_l = (T_abn - T_nor)/||T_abn - T_nor||; zero-shot score s = <f_j/||f_j||, u_l>; z = (s - median_supp)/MAD_supp; few-shot branch standardised the same way; both mapped by a logistic to [0, 1]. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, and stability of the operating threshold across held-out modalities.
RATIONALE: MVFA's zero-shot branch is a two-way softmax over text anchors, so by Do Words Matter? its scale is fixed by the length of the anchor difference times the feature norm, a quantity that is constant per level and known without any test image. The two branches can then be put on a common scale analytically: express the zero-shot branch as the projection on the unit anchor-difference direction, and standardise it and the few-shot branch with support LOO statistics on that projection. This replaces test-set min-max with a geometry-derived, inductive normaliser and keeps 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
METHOD: 1) utils.py: anchor_direction(text_features) per level. 2) test_few.py: zero-shot map = projection on u_l; support LOO median and MAD per branch and level; logistic map; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: none; no training.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std; fusion weight 0.5 and max pooling unchanged in every variant. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max) and the percentile normaliser of the problem statement (1st/99th percentiles of leave-one-out support patch scores). Motivating measurement for all variants: AUROC spread of the transductive pipeline over random half-size test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, spread of realised specificity across held-out datasets. Falsified if the threshold spread is not reduced.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
response:
REASONING: Idea B is distinctly stronger because it targets the precise architectural mechanism causing the scaling mismatch in MVFA—namely the bounded two-way text softmax versus the unbounded few-shot memory distances—and analytically aligns them via anchor-difference projection and robust LOO standardization. In contrast, Idea A relies on generic heuristic add-ons (synthetic Poisson lesion pasting and positional grids) that assume spatial alignment and fail to address the mathematical discrepancy between MVFA's zero-shot and few-shot branches.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH
WINNER=B
